cheng: quick summary from the 3h autotune sweep on the prod farm :eyes:
cheng: observed a reproducible perf regression on a subset of sm86 nodes when sequences float into the 128-512 window
cheng: root cause looks like capability detection mis-classifying fp8/bf16 tensorcore suitability -> falling back to the slow generic kernel (5-6ms/token) instead of the fused tc kernel (~0.9ms/token)
ops-bot: deploy 2026.03.17-rls-97 finished canary rollout @ 09:12 UTC
maya: can you paste the minimal repro and the profiler sample?
cheng: pasted below (sanitized):
```
# autotune command
python tools/autotune.py --farm prod-sm86 --seqlen-range 16,1024 --runs 300 --out=/tmp/auto-sm86.json
# sample profiler snippet (median of 100 runs)
seqlen=128 gpu=sm86 driver=537.21
chosen_kernel: generic_attention
latency: 5.21 ms/token
expected_fast_kernel: tc_fused_attention
expected_latency: 0.92 ms/token
kv_cache_evictions: 12 spikes over 1000 requests
```
cheng: NOTE: the detection log shows we toggled between `tc_fused` and `generic` during the run because the hw-signature fingerprint matched tensorcore heuristics in ~60% of probes and failed in others (driver minor-version behaviour + small timing jitter)
samir: that's the classic flapping case. if our capability signature is a single boolean we get noisy decisions during runtime and that will cause kernel thrash + KV cache pressure
samir: two quick fixes: 1) add hysteresis to signature decisions (persist an inferred capability for N minutes or N runs) 2) make kernel routing sequence-length aware (prefer generic for mid-lengths when memory pressure + kv-evict risk is high)
maya: +1 on hysteresis. also can we tag telemetry with the exact kernel-route so we can query historical route counts per node? currently it's ambiguous
elen: on telemetry: I'll add labels `kernel_route`, `cap_signature_version`, `driver_build` to the selection event. that should help compute p95 route-change rates per machine
cheng: proposing a concrete change set:
- change capability detector to emit (capability, confidence) instead of bool
- delay switching routes until confidence > 0.8 OR persisted decision window of 5m/50 requests
- add seq_len gating: use `fused_tc` for seq<=64 or seq>=1024, use `mid_generic_opt` for 128-512 (this is a cheaper fusion-less kernel tuned for kv cache locality)
- emit `kernel.route.v2` telemetry to tracing pipeline
samir: implementation notes: confidence can be computed from the vector of checks we already run (sm version, tensor core probe microbenchmark, bf16 int8 sanity run). weight driver version higher since we've seen driver bumps flip behaviour
cheng: found an interesting microbench: small microprobe for tensorcore: `cuda_mlp_probe(seed=42, n=1024, iterations=50)` returns 1.3x faster on tc path on some nodes, but the same probe run sometimes times out on a node with the same SM because of a driver scheduling bug
sre-oncall: logging an incident for the production regression spikes: INC-2026-042 (note: no user-facing error, just higher p95 latency on inference tier)
maya: can we quickly roll a canary with the hysteresis toggle only? that should be low risk and buys breathing room for the seq_len gating changes
samir: yes. plan: add a feature flag `runtime.capdetect.hysteresis=5m` default off. canary group = 5% of prod-sm86 for 12h. also enable extra telemetry (elen's labels) for that group
cheng: attached the raw perf dump to the bug (link redacted). key metric to watch: kernel_route_switches_per_node and p95 token latency over 10m windows
elen: I'll add dashboards and an alert: if kernel_route_switches_per_node > 3 in 10m AND p95_token_latency delta > 2x from baseline -> page eng-runtime oncall
maya: other thought: KV cache eviction pattern looked correlated with route flips. when we switch from fused->generic the KV layout changes and we thrash the cache. need to instrument `kv_cache.eviction_cause` too
samir: agree, also ensure we pause autoscaler decisions when hysteresis is active to avoid compounding effects with scaling down/up during noisy transitions
cheng: test plan (short):
- roll hysteresis flag to 5% canary for sm86 (12h) -> verify switches drop and p95 returns to baseline
- run targeted autotune job that exercises seqlen 16..2048 for 1k queries while logging kernel.route and kv.evictions -> offline analysis for mid-range behavior
- if stable, deploy seq_len gating change with a separate feature flag and run AB test for 24h
samir: I'll take the canary rollout + metric checks. assigned to @samir :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all. please paste the canary link once started and the query for `kernel_route_switches_per_node`
ops-bot: scheduled job `autotune-sm86-midrange` started at 11:03 UTC (job id: 94c2)
cheng: thanks, I'll follow the job and try to reproduce locally with a pinned driver container
elen: creating telemetry PR now, will tag it in this thread
cheng: action items: samir (canary + checks), elen (telemetry labels + alert), maya (kv eviction instrumentation), cheng (local repro + microprobe hardening) :shipit:
